title: Idempotent lifting for the structure sheaf over a henselian pair
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, let $Z\to S$ be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $Z_0=Z\times_SS_0$ with its projection $i:Z_0\to Z$. Then:

(a) $W\mapsto W_0=W\times_SS_0=i^{-1}(W)$ is a bijection from the set of open and closed subsets of $Z$ to the set of open and closed subsets of $Z_0$. In particular an open and closed subset $W\subseteq Z$ with $W\times_SS_0=\emptyset$ is empty.

(b) Restriction $i^\sharp:H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ induces a bijection between the idempotents of the two rings: every idempotent of $H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

(The map $i^\sharp$ itself need not be bijective: for $A=k[[t]]$, $I=(t)$, $Z=\mathbf P^1_A$ it is $k[[t]]\to k$.)

proof.text: Restrict clopen subsets to the closed fibre using lem-weil-pbc-henselian-clopen-restriction, the first three steps of the previous proof. This supplies injectivity and a clopen lift of each closed-fibre clopen.

*Step 4 (statement (b)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent] (b), $e\mapsto U_e$ is a bijection from the idempotents of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ to the open and closed subsets of $Z$, and likewise for $Z_0$; by (c) of that lemma applied to $g=i$, $i^\sharp(e)$ is idempotent and $U_{i^\sharp(e)}=i^{-1}(U_e)$. So the map $e\mapsto i^\sharp(e)$ on idempotents is, through these two bijections, the map $W\mapsto i^{-1}(W)$ of Step 3, which is bijective. Hence $i^\sharp$ is bijective on idempotents: every idempotent of $H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ is $i^\sharp(e)$ for exactly one idempotent $e$ of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.21.3 (Tag 00EE) for the correspondence on affine pieces; the passage to idempotents written out by the agent

proof.text: For injectivity, equal restricted idempotents have equal clopen loci on Y₀. Pullback compatibility identifies these with inverse images of their loci on Y, so clopen injectivity gives equal loci, and scheme_clopen_idempotent gives equal idempotents. For surjectivity, lift the locus of a closed-fibre idempotent to a clopen U on Y, realize U by an idempotent e, and use pullback compatibility and injectivity of the closed-fibre locus map to identify the restriction of e with the given idempotent.
